passages.text: Therefore, neither are the Hebrews condemned for not knowing Jesus, because of the one who hid him, provided that, while doing the things through Moses .... they do not hate the one they did not know; nor, in turn, are those from the nations who did not know Moses condemned because of the one who concealed him, provided that they too, while doing the things spoken through Jesus, do not hate the one they did not know. Nor do people gain any benefit by calling their teachers “lords” while not performing servants’ duties. For this reason, our Jesus said to someone who repeatedly called him Lord but did nothing that he commanded: “Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and not do what I say?” For saying will not benefit anyone, but doing will. In every way, therefore, good works are needed. Yet if anyone should be deemed worthy to recognize both of them as proclaiming one teaching, that man has been counted rich in God, having understood the ancient things to be new with respect to time and the new things to be old.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantival phrase means the things characteristic of servants. In accordance with the reader-facing wording policy, δούλων is rendered “servants,” but it can denote slaves or owned or bonded servants; the contrast with “lords” invokes their subordinate status and obligations.
The comparative adverb can mean “more frequently” or, idiomatically, “rather frequently”; the context emphasizes repeated address.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοὺς ἀμφοτέρους ἐπιγνῶναι ὡς μιᾶς διδασκαλίας ὑπ’ αὐτῶν κεκηρυγμένης
lexical_decisions.chosen: to recognize both of them as proclaiming one teaching
lexical_decisions.rationale: This renders the teaching proclaimed by both as the basis or content of recognizing them together. The ὡς with the genitive absolute may alternatively be represented more explicitly as “to recognize both of them, inasmuch as one teaching has been proclaimed by them.”
The idiom stresses necessity by every consideration; “by all means” is an alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τά τε ἀρχαῖα νέα τῷ χρόνῳ καὶ τὰ καινὰ παλαιὰ ὄντα
lexical_decisions.chosen: the ancient things to be new with respect to time and the new things to be old
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering preserves the printed paradox. τῷ χρόνῳ may alternatively be understood as “with time” or “in relation to time.”

source_issues.source_quote: ἐάν γε πράττοντες τὰ διὰ Μωϋσέως .... ὃν ἠγνόησαν μὴ μισήσωσιν
source_issues.issue: The selected image-checked edition contains a confirmed four-dot printed lacuna after “the things through Moses.” Its lost content and precise syntactic contribution are unavailable, so the four dots are retained exactly and no restoration is supplied. This prevents recovery of the complete lost wording but does not block publication of a translation explicitly representing the selected edition’s surviving text and printed gap.
